channel.title: Sheherazade's Lantern
channel.description: Ancient tales from the Arabian nights, rekindled for modern souls — anime-style audio drama with full voice cast. Journey across the Silk Road with the Lantern Keeper as your guide.
channel.itunes:author: The Lantern Keeper
channel.itunes:summary: Ancient tales from the Arabian nights, rekindled for modern souls — anime-style audio drama with full voice cast.

item.title: The Map of the Moving Streets
item.description: Rashid the Mapmaker draws cities that change overnight. Yueya the astronomer discovers his maps match a sky that hasn't risen yet. Together they find the Brass City — built by King Solomon's djinn.

item.title: The Spice of Forgotten Things
item.description: A city is forgetting itself. Karim meets Nadia the Spice Merchant, who offers him a taste of every life he never lived.

item.title: The Blade That Was Never Finished
item.description: A haunted swordsmith. A boy seeking revenge. An unfinished blade on the wall. Khalid keeps a secret that the forge fire cannot burn away.

item.title: The Book of Things Never Said
item.description: Once a century, a door appears in the Caravanserai. Inside waits Dunyazad, Scheherazade's sister, with a book of blank pages that holds every unspoken truth.

item.title: The Sand That Sang Twice
item.description: Deep in the Empty Quarter, Karim hears the dunes singing. Layla holds a single grain of sand that reveals what he has been searching for his entire life.

item.title: The Spice That Remembered
item.description: Nadia finds a black peppercorn that opens a door to the Black Bazaar — a market that exists between worlds. She and Rashid enter together, and discover that the most precious thing in the shadow market isn't for sale: it's the memory of something you lost before you were born.

item.title: The Song That Unmade a Sword
item.description: Layla of the Singing Dunes arrives at Khalid's forge with a single grain of sand that carries a melody from before the world was made. The song has the power to finish what he started forty years ago — but only if he is willing to let his unfinished blade be broken first.
